outcome: A linked, instrumented DiscStudio with editable domain-bound presentations and reusable competition Constraints.

requirements.text: Named bags use shared physical-disc references
Drafts, photos and changes survive reload
Every field is discoverable; identity text is editable
One presentation works for Single and DiscBattle
Compose on footage, export a transparent overlay
Independent states, scores, highlights and winner
Real PQL path and memoized Parts are inspectable
Item comments persist and export with checkpoint identity
The composition exports its own pyto-run-record@1 and opens a Tick render
requirements.reviewRoute: OnTheCourse (#/course?trace=1) with the sample workspace: press “Export run record ↓”, expect a downloaded pyto-run-record@1 the shared validator accepted and the Part px.run.on-the-course (14 Ticks, one invocation per PQL Calculation); press “Open Tick render ↗”, expect a saved standalone page that opens over file:// with no server and shows one section per Tick.
requirements.verification: Verified by npm test (tests/core.test.js: the record validates, one Tick per composition Tick, the receipt's material digests reach it, composePage's page round-trips the record and renders one section per Tick), node --test pyto/viewer/test/*.test.mjs, and scripts/browser_test.py --embedded, whose new block drives the studio on a real local origin and opens the saved page over file:// with zero network requests. Deployed build: scripts/build.mjs now copies pyto/viewer/ into dist/ because src/app.js and src/runtime.js import it directly; npm run build confirms dist/pyto/viewer/ exists. The deployed page itself has not been opened in a browser. Automated verification only; no human acceptance is recorded.

requirements.text: The studio reads its own receipts through PQL, and undo is one more Calculation on the record
requirements.reviewRoute: OnTheCourse (#/course?trace=1) with the sample workspace: press “Inspect PxC ↗” and read the Receipts section, expect one row per px.receipt.* Part with its name, consumes, produces and result digest; on the Shelf, press “↶ Undo last change”, expect the exact previous workspace back and a studio-undo row in that same list.
requirements.verification: Verified by npm test (tests/core.test.js: `into` may be an array and both Parts are published or neither is, the px.receipt.* prefix query is answered sorted, the Receipts rows and summary are the two Parts one Calculation publishes, push/pop restores the exact previous value, a pop on an empty stack is a recorded no-op, and the run record carries the undo invocations), node --test pyto/viewer/test/*.test.mjs, and scripts/browser_test.py --embedded, whose eleventh check drives the Undo button and compares the rendered rows against px.receipt.* in the store and whose twelfth runs the sample composition with parallel: true, reads parallel, placement, latency_ms and budget off the exported record and checks the Tick page draws that Tick's branches on one row. scripts/review_checkpoint.mjs pins the count at 12. Automated verification only; no human acceptance is recorded.

checkpoints.summary: Ported painter disc-art Calculation and deterministic shelf-sheet Calculation are available for review.

checkpoints.summary: Several `into` per Calculation and a px.receipt.* prefix query in the PQL grammar; a Receipts section on Inspect built from them; px.undo.<scope> with fn.undo.push/pop/settle and an Undo button on the Shelf card.
checkpoints.verification: npm test, node --test pyto/viewer/test/*.test.mjs and scripts/browser_test.py --embedded all pass; the browser checks are now 12 and scripts/review_checkpoint.mjs pins that count.

resume: CI emits an exact-commit item/submission under dist/review after fresh tests. Review each item in the in-app neat checklist, export comments, and address those items. No human acceptance is implied.
